extracted.intended_audience: researchers, journal editors, publication-ethics professionals, and stakeholders interested in post-publication peer review (PPPR) and platform governance
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and considerations for assessing post-publication peer review (PPPR) platforms (e.g., PubPeer), including their purpose, benefits, vulnerabilities, and the policy/technical measures needed to ensure constructive, equitable scientific discourse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and character of PPPR
rubrics_metrics.description: PPPR is defined as a critical, ongoing, and public review conducted by the broader scientific community once research findings are formally published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes that PPPR should allow more academic experts to continuously examine, question, and validate published work; this ongoing dialogue promotes transparency and motivates authors to make necessary corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary goals and benefits of PPPR
rubrics_metrics.description: To identify errors and encourage authors to make necessary corrections; to enable continuous expert examination of work that may have been missed during initial review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame PPPR as a tool that safeguards science by supporting continuous review of scientific knowledge, facilitating detection of flaws and strengths post-publication, and promoting transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive criticism versus hyper-skepticism
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguishes constructive criticism (which fosters understanding) from 'hyper-skepticism', an overly critical mindset that focuses on doubt rather than fostering understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocates for criticism that aims to clarify and improve science rather than insistently doubt or attack; identify and discourage hyper-skeptic behaviors that do not contribute constructively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vulnerabilities to misuse and weaponization
rubrics_metrics.description: The open nature of PPPR platforms makes them vulnerable to misuse; they can be exploited to undermine colleagues, suppress differing viewpoints, or further personal or organizational interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be alert to signs of targeted attacks, suppression of legitimate dissent, or agenda-driven critiques; consider moderation, provenance, and conflict-of-interest controls to reduce weaponization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for an equitable and responsible PPPR framework
rubrics_metrics.description: To fully realize PPPR benefits and prevent misuse, the scientific community must build a more equitable and more responsible framework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calls for thoughtful strategy development involving multiple stakeholders (scientists, editors, platforms) to balance openness with safeguards for fair debate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technological measures to support PPPR
rubrics_metrics.description: Integration of technological advancements is necessary as part of a comprehensive strategy to realize PPPR's benefits and prevent misuse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied measures include platform design choices (identity/attribution, moderation tools, provenance tracking, detection of coordinated attacks) though specifics are not provided in the preview; technology should support transparency and integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengthened editorial policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial policies should be enhanced to address issues arising from PPPR activity and its potential for misuse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journals/editors need clearer policies for responding to PPPR critiques, investigating concerns, protecting authors from bad-faith attacks, and coordinating with platforms when substantive problems are raised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increased transparency measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Transparency measures should be enhanced to improve the quality and accountability of PPPR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency could include clearer disclosure of commenters' identities or conflicts, transparent handling of allegations, and openness about editorial actions taken in response to PPPR; specifics implied but not detailed in abstract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections for good-faith scientific debate
rubrics_metrics.description: Robust protections are needed to safeguard legitimate scientific discourse on PPPR platforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protective measures should preserve the ability of researchers to engage in good-faith critique while minimizing harassment, reputational harm, or suppression of honest disagreement; suggested as part of an integrated strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of the scientific community in governance
rubrics_metrics.description: The scientific community must participate in building governance that balances openness with responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages community-driven solutions and stakeholder engagement (including editors, researchers, and platform operators) to design fair, effective PPPR practices and policies.
